summary: 6 batch-50 preflight exclusions, originally attributed to a mechanical pretty-printer proof-elision failure (printed type contains an unparseable `⋯`), reclassified after a 29 July 2026 characterization session showed the print failure is recoverable (`pp.proofs true` makes all 6 re-elaborate cleanly). The mechanical failure is therefore NOT the load-bearing reason these 6 stay excluded. The actual, recorded reason: all 6 are dependent recursion/elimination principles -- proof infrastructure whose content is Lean encoding rather than a described mathematical object. Dossiers would underdetermine little (the definition IS its own type signature), fact supply is near-tautological (defining equations collapse to self-restatements), and casework/membership regimes are vacuous for this shape. They rank well on the richness metric precisely because dependent binders/arrows are what that metric counts -- a known metric blind spot (see docs/deferred.md), not evidence these are good task targets.
provisional_note: This is a curation call on 6 names (~1% of the 727-eligible corpus), not a coded miner gate. If eliminator/recursor-shaped definitions surface at meaningful scale in a wider harvest, this decision gets re-evaluated against that evidence rather than standing on today's small sample. See docs/deferred.md.
batch_50_context: The 3 OTHER original preflight exclusions (WithTop.subtypeOrderIso: stuck typeclass metavariable; Equiv.sigmaSigmaSubtypeEq: REPL server crash on validation; Finset.sumLift₂: subscript character invalid as a Lean identifier for the task symbol) are unchanged by this decision and keep their original mechanical reasons -- they are not part of this quarantine file. The batch-50 selection remains 41 names.

names.name: Nat.leRec
names.description: Recursion starting at an arbitrary base n rather than 0: given a value/proof for n and a step showing motive k -> motive (k+1) for every k >= n, produces motive m for any m >= n.
names.mechanical_exclusion_recovery_note: pp.proofs true removes the ellipsis (prints Nat.le_refl n / Nat.le_succ_of_le h in place of ⋯); the resulting full text re-elaborates cleanly as `def VTask.leRec : <type> := sorry` against the warm environment. Verified 29 July 2026. The pretty-printer failure is therefore known-recoverable and is NOT why this name stays excluded.
names.curation_reason: eliminator/recursor: content is encoding; dossier underdetermines little; fact supply near-tautological

names.name: SimpleGraph.Walk.mapToSubgraph

names.mechanical_exclusion_recovery_note: Structural variant of the same cause -- the elided proof term sits inside an anonymous-constructor Subtype literal in the return type, not a direct motive argument. pp.proofs true resolves it (prints the two named membership proofs); re-elaborates cleanly.
